In sales, you are always taught to go for up sells or add-ons. I've worked a few sales jobs, and they are always big about add on. Think about the last time you bought a DVD at wal-mart. The disc, I mean, not a player. The cashier will ask you if you want a protection plan for it that will replace it for 2 years is something happens to it.

Repair chains around here figure in Add-Ons as part of their base price. I bought new tires at Discount Tire for my jeep. I researched them online and knew how much they were going to cost, how much the mounting and balancing were going to be and how much the disposal fee would be. When I checked out and was paying, it was like $200 more. I asked him about it and he said that's the regular price for the tires, the warranty, mounting, balancing, disposable and the mounting kit.

I said, wait a sec, what warranty, he said the road hazard warranty and I told him I didn't want any warranty except what the manufacturer provides. He told me I should get it, I said naw, kill it. So he did. That knocked about $125 off but it was still high. I asked him what was the mounting kit, I thought stems were included in the cost of mounting. He said they were, the mounting kit was a new set of blah blah anti-theft lug-nuts. I said I didn't ask for those. He said "oh, well they are already on there" I said cool so, unless they are free, you have 5 mins to get them off and put mine back or I'm considering them free. He got the manager and I told him no dice, put mine back. They had trouble finding mine so I said I'm not paying $75 bucks for the lug nuts. They found them after a bit and replaces them.

Another time, I had it in for an alignment. They wanted like $190 for the alignment and I asked what all they were going to adjust. The said they would put it on the machine and fully adjust castor, camber, thrust and toe. I said "umm, you've guys worked on wranglers, right?" he said yeah, all the time. So I asked them how would they adjust castor and camber. He said they would replace the shims and adjust some bolts to line it up to spec. I'm like umm no thanks, that has a solid front axle, the only adjustment points are toe and thrust angle and thrust is only adjustable if it's been modified.

I've had a friend that was complaining that shops were charging her $400 bucks to replace the transmission filter and fluid in her 350z. I asked when it would be done and she told me later that day. I said I would go with her. She went to pick it up and they were detailing all the work they did and had asked her for payment and I said hang on a sec. Looked at the invoice and sure enough they did. I asked the guy to come over to the car with me. I opened the door and pointed out that it had a clutch and a stick. He said, yeah, and? So I popped the hood and asked him to show me where they put the transmission fluid and he pointed to the clutch reservoir. I told her not to pay them shit. They said they wouldn't be giving her the keys then, and I said ok, I'll call the cops and see if we can get them get them to release the car. He let her have it and the manager called her the next day saying that the guy had mixed up the invoicing.

I guess the point is, a shop will say here's what we can do. It's really up to you to determine if that is necessary. Remember, that make money off of your stress.
